text:
mei: Heads-up — during int8 bring-up of model v2.1-compact we see a regression on CJK coverage hits vs fp16. Quick summary: ~7.2% drop in subword coverage on our kanji/hangul mixed set, and many multi-script tokens are being split into unexpected subtokens.

raj: :eyes: can you paste an example tokenization? is this the tokenizer change or the quantization artifacts?

mei: Example (expected single token): `漢字한글` -> expected `[\u6f22\u5b57한글]` as one subword, got tokenized to `漢` `字` `한` `글` (4 tokens). Another failing case: `「東京-서울」` becomes `「` `東京` `-` `首` `尔` `」` (weird split in Seoul).

anya: that's odd — looks like sentencepiece merges are different. Did we re-create the tokenizer with the new vocab file?

mei: We used the same vocab blob (vocab_2024-09) but the tokenization binary came from the quantized model package (we ship a tiny tokenizer C++ binary). I ran `strings tokenizer.bin | head` and the merge table checksum differs from the repo one.

build-bot: CI: tokenizer build completed (sha: a1b2c3) — artifact uploaded to s3://redwood-inference-artifacts/tokenizer/1878654/tokenizer.bin

raj: hmm if the binary differs that could indicate a packaging bug. But the coverage drop is also observable when using Python tokenizers pointed at the same vocab?

mei: I ran the python tokenization (sentencepiece v0.1.96) against `vocab_2024-09.model` and it matches fp16 outputs. The regression only appears when using the packaged C++ binary that ships with int8 runtime.

olga: Could quantization have changed default normalization or unicode NFKC/NFC behavior at serialization? We've seen NFKC toggles affect CJK joins before.

mei: Good call — diffed `tokenizer.bin` strings: the binary has `normalization: NFC` while repo model uses `NFKC`. That would explain some joins turning into separate codepoints.

anya: That explains some of the splits, but what about the 7.2% coverage delta? Are we counting coverage as fraction of characters mapped to single subword?

mei: Coverage metric we use: percent of CJK tokens with token_count==1 on our kanji/hangul mixed dev set. fp16 baseline = 89.7%, int8 packaged runtime = 82.5%.

raj: Ok, two-pronged problem: (1) packaging step replaced normalization, (2) maybe tokenizer binary build flags or sentencepiece version differs. For the quantization angle: did you try running the same packaged tokenizer but with fp16 model (no quant) to isolate?

mei: Yes. Packaged tokenizer + fp16 model -> still low coverage (~82.6%). So it's a tokenizer packaging issue, not numeric quantization.

qa-bot: EVAL: ran quick translation quality test on small kanji-hangul set — BLEU drop -1.6, chrF -3.2 relative to baseline. Narrowed to samples where token_count>1 increased.

olga: We'll fix the tokenizer packaging first. But also let's audit the eval harness: do we penalize models that produce extra tokens at score-time? Some rerankers use token-level features that may over-penalize.

mei: Plan: (1) revert tokenizer binary to use repo normalization (NFKC) and rebuild artifacts, (2) add small unit test with mixed-script examples, (3) run full quantized bring-up after tokenizer fix.

santiago: I'll own the packaging pipeline change. Possible culprit: upstream sentencepiece build default changed between 0.1.94 and 0.1.96 which our build container now picks up. Pinning sentencepiece in the build container should stabilize.

anya: Also add a chokepoint check in our release checklist: `tokenization-smoke` that runs these 50 mixed-script examples and fails the package if coverage delta > 0.5% from baseline.

raj: Good. As a secondary follow-up: once tokenizer is fixed, re-run int8 vs fp16 quant experiments to confirm no accuracy regressions introduced by quant kernel selection. Log per-layer activation histograms and per-head attention sparsity stats.

mei: I'll push a patch to packaging and trigger a rebuild. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizer/pull/482 — includes test vectors and pin to sentencepiece 0.1.94.

santiago: Starting a rebuild now. Will post artifact link when done. :rocket:

build-bot: CI: rebuild started for tokenizer@1878654-patch — logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/logs/1878654

mei: Thanks. If this closes, then our quant bring-up stays on schedule. If not, we'll escalate to infra for container rollback.

olga: Also add a note to the onboarding playbook about verifying normalization flags during model bring-up. Learned that the tokenizer binary is a single point of failure for multilingual quality.

raj: Thanks team — let's sync tomorrow if rebuild doesn't clear the regression.

santiago: build done — artifact uploaded s3://redwood-inference-artifacts/tokenizer/1878654/tokenizer.bin (sha: d4e5f6). Preliminary local check: mixed-script coverage back to 89.8%.

mei: Awesome — running the full eval now.

qa-bot: EVAL: full run queued (job 1878655).
